answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 14 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The horizon multiplier is published, charged in dawn, and ember lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 1585 identities would post 4017 proofs and burn roughly 51 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
